conviction_note: Small long lean: the EPS bar ($0.03-0.05) sits well below the CFO's own normalized Q2 run-rate (~$23m operating income) and last year's Q3 $0.10, the new Maker 5 flagship shipped inside the quarter, tariff rates are lower y/y, and the name has risen on 6 of its last 7 prints into an all-Sell, 3-analyst bar with 7.8 days to cover. Against that, revenue missed in Q1 and Q2, Q3 subscriber softness was pre-guided, and the last Q3 print (Nov 2025) fell 5% on an EPS beat. Hence p_up 57 on a 10% absolute move gives +1.4, equal to the +1.4 sum of the findings. The two agree in sign and size by coincidence, not by fitting.
bar: Revenue ~$171-174m. Zacks $170.97m and therighttrader $172.0m roughly agree; Earnings Whispers $173.7m (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/CRCT/21559); Chartmill $176.6m and Tickflow $165m are outliers. EPS is disputed: $0.03 (Earnings Whispers) against $0.05 (Chartmill, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/CRCT/estimates). FY2026 consensus revenue is $696.7m (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/crct/forecast/), which with H1 at $315.8m implies H2 $380.9m, +1.8% y/y. Q3 2025 comparison: revenue $170.4m, of which platform $82.8m and products $87.7m, EPS ~$0.10 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1828962/000182896225000151/cricutq32025earningsrelease.htm). No formal company guide. On the Q2 call management said 'we project growth in the second half on products and platform' and that platform will grow each quarter (https://www.webull.com/news/15386993160774656). Consensus roughly sits inside that qualitative guide. Because EPS is single-sourced and disputed, the EPS finding is capped small.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest via Equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/crct/short-interest): 4,411,918 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 7.80 days to cover, down from 4.94m on 09-15. That is about 2.1% of total shares, but roughly 8% of the ~54.7m Class A shares, since most of the company is Class B held by the controlling holder. Sell-side: 3 covering analysts, all Sell (Barclays $4, Goldman $4.50, Morgan Stanley $3.70), consensus 'Strong Sell' with a $4.07 average target against $6.05 spot (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/crct/forecast/). No usable option chain (empty_chain), so there is no skew. Run-up -5.2% over 20 days and -1.6% over 5, spot 9.7% below the 52-week high. The bearish sell-side bar plus a moderately crowded short is a mechanism for upside on any beat.

findings.finding: Cricut launched its flagship Cricut Maker 5 on 2026-09-04, inside Q3. It was exclusive to Cricut.com and Michaels for two weeks and then went to other retailers (Kohl's lists the bundles, 4.6 stars on 98 reviews), so the launch sell-in lands in Q3 products revenue. Consensus of ~$171-174m implies products of only ~$84-87m against $87.7m a year earlier (-1% to -4%) if platform grows ~5% to ~$87m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Products revenue fell 22% in Q2 2026 and 9.6% in Q1 2026, both revenue misses, yet the stock rose +22.9% and +5.2%. Q3 2025 products fell 3% with connected machines up 12%, and the stock fell -5.2% on 'slow revenue growth'. The products line has not driven the sign recently.
findings.why_not_priced: The previews quote a flat y/y revenue consensus, which embeds a products decline. Had the market priced a launch-driven products return to growth, consensus would sit above $175m and the 3-analyst Sell bar would have moved. Targets were last set 08-05 to 09-10, around or before the launch, and have not moved since.
findings.independence: Management on the Q2 call: 'we project growth in the second half on products and platform' and 'additional launches coming' (https://www.webull.com/news/15386993160774656). Retail listing: https://www.kohls.com/product/prd-8711913/cricut-maker-5-essential-bundle-cutting-machine.jsp. This sits inside management's qualitative H2 guide, so it is partly expected. Net of the rest: accessories and materials eroded (-17% in Q3 2025) and ASPs fell on a lower-priced machine mix. Those can absorb the launch.

findings.finding: The Q3 EPS bar of $0.03 (Earnings Whispers) to $0.05 (Chartmill) is well below the CFO's stated normalized Q2 run-rate (gross margin ~58.9%, operating income ~$23m, 14.7% margin excluding the refund and royalty one-offs), which works out to ~$0.09 a share after tax and interest income. It is also below Q3 2025 actual EPS of ~$0.10. The sell-side has under-forecast EPS for several quarters: Q2 actual $0.19 against $0.04, Q3 2025 $0.10 against $0.04.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There were large EPS beats on Q3 2025 (-5.2%), Q4 2025 (+4.6%), Q1 2026 (+5.2%) and Q2 2026 (+22.9%). The EPS beat is habitual and has been bought 3 of the last 4 times, but the one prior Q3 was sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Three Sell-rated analysts keep the estimate near $0.03-0.05 despite the company's own normalized disclosure. If the market priced ~$0.09, the published consensus would be near there. Some of the gap is plausibly H2 marketing ramp and AI cost, which management flagged.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 8-K actual net income of $20.5m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1828962/000182896225000151/cricutq32025earningsrelease.htm). The EPS bar is disputed between sources, so this finding is capped. It shares the margin driver with the tariff finding below.

findings.finding: Tariff cost is lower y/y in Q3. The Supreme Court ruled IEEPA tariffs unauthorized on 2026-02-20, a 10% Section 122 surcharge then ran to 2026-07-24, and a 12.5% Section 301 layer applies since, against the higher IEEPA China stack that weighed on Q3 2025's 55.2% gross margin. The 10-Q also shows $1.7m of approved refunds sitting in inventory that flows through cost of revenue as the stock sells, plus a $3.5m refund receivable.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 gross margin of 74.5% was flattered by a $17.9m refund, and the stock rose +22.9%, though the CFO's normalized margin of 58.9% was flat y/y.
findings.why_not_priced: Management declined to guide margin ('existing tariffs remain a headwind'), so models carry no y/y tariff relief. If the market priced it, the EPS consensus would sit above Q3 2025's $0.10 rather than below it.
findings.independence: Proxy for the tariff schedule: https://borderbuddy.com/trade-tariff-news/section-122-is-out-section-301-is-in. That is macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed. The 10-Q also cites Middle East fuel and petrochemical input cost pressure, which offsets part of it.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-22 Cricut signed a new 5-year $300m senior secured revolver with BMO, replacing its 2022 JPMorgan facility, on which no principal was outstanding. The stated purposes include share repurchases and permitted acquisitions, with dividends and buybacks uncapped at pro forma net leverage of 2.5x or less. Combined with ~$286m of cash and securities and no debt, this is capacity for capital return, not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Specials have been declared in May (2024 $0.40, 2025 $0.75) and December 2022 ($0.35). The October/November declarations have been the regular $0.10 only (Nov 1 2024, Oct 31 2025). The buyback had ~$21.6m left at June 30.
findings.why_not_priced: It was a quiet Item 1.01 8-K with no press release. If the market read it as a precursor to a replenished buyback, special dividend or acquisition, there would be wire coverage. Asked what the money buys: nothing is drawn and the use is optional, so the sign is mildly positive and the size small.
findings.independence: The dividend history in the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001828962/000182896226000049/crct-20260630.htm). Management: 'subject to stock price, we also expect to be active with our authorized $50 million stock repurchase program' (https://www.webull.com/news/15386993160774656). No 8-K dividend declaration is visible on EDGAR yet this year, though last year's came on Oct 31.

findings.finding: Management pre-guided Q3 subscriber softness ('normal seasonality could still see flat to declining quarter-on-quarter subscriber growth rates'). Paid subscribers grew only 3% y/y in Q2 (3.103m) against 6% in Q3 2025, so a flat or down q/q print against 3.004m a year ago is the expected outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 was sold -5.2% on 'slow revenue growth' despite subscribers +6%. Subscriber stabilization was cited as a positive in Q2 2026 (+22.9%).
findings.why_not_priced: This is largely priced because it was guided. It is filed because a q/q decline in paid subscribers would be the first visible crack in the platform story the stock re-rated on in August.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K subscriber table (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001828962/000182896226000048/cricutq22026earningsrelease.htm). Same call as the EPS finding.

findings.finding: Revenue missed consensus in both Q1 2026 ($159.5m, about $4.9m short) and Q2 2026 ($156.3m against ~$160-164m), with products down 9.6% and 22%. Accessories and materials erosion and heavier promotions (10-Q) are structural, so the Q3 top line risks a third consecutive miss against ~$171-174m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Both 2026 revenue misses were bought (+5.2%, +22.9%). The Q3 2025 revenue disappointment was sold (-5.2%).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The consensus was not cut below flat y/y even after two misses. A market expecting a third miss would show a consensus near $165m (only Tickflow is there).
findings.independence: Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001828962/000182896226000048/cricutq22026earningsrelease.htm). This is the offset to the Maker 5 finding, and both rest on the products line.

findings.finding: The sell-side is uniformly bearish (3 of 3 Sell, $4.07 average target, 33% below spot) while 4.41m shares are short at 7.8 days to cover (2026-10-15). The stock has closed up on 6 of its last 7 prints, three of them by 17-23%.
findings.why_not_priced: Without an option chain there is no priced directional statement. The asymmetric reaction history and a short base above 7 days to cover mean a non-disappointing print forces covering. The short base fell from 4.94m to 4.41m over the month, so some covering has already happened.

findings.finding: CEO Ashish Arora has sold 60,000 shares roughly every two weeks since 2026-08-05 under a Rule 10b5-1 plan (latest 10-21 at $6.31 and 10-23 at $6.26), leaving 5.03m shares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Arora has also sold through earlier prints, e.g. a June 2025 sale, and the stock still rose on prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The sales are scheduled and public on Form 4. They are filed for completeness, as a pre-set plan, not as a signal.

rejected_candidates.detail: The 10-Q notes Q4 is 29% of revenue with heavier promotions (Q4 2025 GM 47%). Any Q4 commentary is covered by the H2 products and guidance discussion in the Maker 5 and revenue-miss findings; no dated Q4 data found.

baseline_tension: There is no option skew. The 20-day run-up is mildly negative (-5.2%) and the stock sits 10% off its high, with up-reactions on 6 of 7 prints. The small long lean agrees with the reaction history and the crowded-ish short, and cuts against the uniformly bearish sell-side targets.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the EPS consensus is single-sourced and disputed ($0.03 against $0.05), so the EPS-bar finding is capped from +0.8 to +0.5.

Lessons 6 and 9 (inside the guide, segment net of the rest): the Maker 5 sell-in lands inside management's 'H2 products growth' claim and must offset accessories erosion, so it moves from +1.0 to +0.8.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage, 3 analysts): abs_move_pct raised from 9 to 10. The baseline mean absolute reaction is ~11.3 and the median 5.2.
Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; the last Q3 EPS beat was sold): p_up moved from 58 to 57.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the revolver is signed positive only after checking its uses (buybacks/M&A, undrawn, no debt). It was already sized so in the draft, so it is unchanged.
Lesson 7: short interest was checked before the negative findings. 7.8 days to cover keeps the negatives small; no change.
